trial_court: Trial Court dated 7.3.1977 in O.S. No.269/1975
case_name: Bharatha Matha & Anr vs R. Vijaya Renganathan & Ors

parties.respondent_defendant: R. Vijaya Renganathan & Ors (wife, husband, defendant)

facts_of_case: Peria Mariammal instituted a suit against respondents claiming the share of her brother Muthu Reddiar. Respondents contested the suit denying the marriage between defendant No.1 and Alagarsami Reddiar. Trial Court decreed the suit recording the finding that Rengammal was wife of Alagarsami Reddiar who was alive at the time of filing the suit.

legal_principles.principle: High Court cannot decide Second Appeal by re-appreciating evidence as if it was deciding First Appeal unless it comes to the conclusion that the findings recorded by the court below were perverse.
legal_principles.held: In Rajappa Hanamantha Ranoji Vs. Mahadev Channabasappa & Ors., this Court held that it is not permissible for the High Court to decide the Second Appeal by re-appreciating the evidence as if it was deciding the First Appeal unless it comes to the conclusion that the findings recorded by the court below were perverse.
cited_cases: Rajappa Hanamantha Ranoji Vs. Mahadev Channabasappa & Ors., (2000) SC 2108

legal_principles.principle: High Court can interfere with the finding of fact while deciding the Second Appeal provided the findings recorded by the Courts below are perverse.
legal_principles.held: Thus, it is evident that High Court can interfere with the finding of fact while deciding the Second Appeal provided the findings recorded by the Courts below are perverse.
cited_cases: Kulwant Kaur & Ors. Vs. Gurdial Singh Mann (dead) by L.Rs., (2001) SC 1273

outcome.final_order: The High Court of Judicature at Madras dated 10th July, 2001 allowing the appeal filed by respondent No.1 against the judgment and decree of the Ist Appellate Court dated 17.9.1986 affirming the judgment and decree of the Trial Court.
